metadata.note: Real progress recap of C:\Users\kavya\OneDrive\Desktop\CabStream, grounded in that repo's actual git log (not illustrative/fabricated). This reel covers WEEK 2 ONLY (commits 2026-06-16 through 2026-06-22, confirmed via `git log --all --format='%ad %h %s' --date=short`): six commits, all on 06-19 and 06-20 (06-16/17/18 and 06-21/22 are silent). 56c17b9 (06-19 18:38): initial Terraform config for Azure infra -- databricks.tf, eventhubs.tf, main.tf, outputs.tf, storage.tf, variables.tf, 262 insertions across 6 files. d3e8959 (06-19 23:00): main.tf/variables.tf expanded (+23 lines). 4475953, 6436b64, 798fc61 (06-19): readme update, .gitignore additions for terraform state/tfvars, terraform lock file (housekeeping). 7d1eef4 (06-20 12:12): fix(infra) -- added a personal user read-only access policy to Key Vault, plus keyvault.tf itself (25 lines) -- this is the week's one real fix, a security/access-control gap found and closed the day after the initial Key Vault resource was defined. Honest scope caveat, directly supported by the file-level evidence: this window only touches terraform/*.tf files -- no application/producer code changed, so the infra is DEFINED AND PLANNED (terraform files committed) but there is no evidence in this git log that `terraform apply` was run or that the week-1 local Kafka pipeline was actually repointed at the new Event Hubs namespace. Built to satisfy docs/FELLOWS-SUBMISSION.md's required-content rules: the required intro line opens B00's narration verbatim, AI-narration is disclosed in the same beat, and this reel renders native 16:9 (3840x2160) and 9:16 (2160x3840).

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my second week building CabStream, a real-time data pipeline project. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Week one was a local Kafka pipeline, running in Docker on my own machine. Week two was something different: the same pipeline, defined as real cloud infrastructure, entirely in code. What actually got built, and why Terraform instead of clicking through the Azure portal?

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: week two wasn't clicking through the Azure portal setting things up by hand. It's six resources, defined entirely in Terraform — reproducible infrastructure, not a one-time setup nobody can repeat.

beats.narration_text: Four things to track. Event Hubs: Azure's managed Kafka, defined to replace the local Docker setup — same producer code, zero infrastructure to run myself. Databricks: a managed Spark workspace, standing in for the cluster I'd otherwise have to tune by hand. Storage and Key Vault, added the same day, so secrets never sit in code. And one real gap, found and closed the very next day.

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual log, not a summary. June nineteenth, six-thirty-eight PM: the first Terraform commit, six files, Event Hubs through Key Vault outputs. Eleven PM the same night: the config gets expanded. June twentieth, noon: the fix — a personal read-only policy added to Key Vault, so I could actually debug what Terraform had built.

beats.narration_text: What week two didn't have yet: no deployment. These are Terraform files, committed and reviewable — not confirmation that terraform apply actually ran, or that any of these resources exist in Azure right now. And the week-one Kafka pipeline hasn't been repointed at Event Hubs — it's still reading from the local Docker setup. The plan exists. It hasn't been run.

beats.narration_text: Recap: six Terraform resources defined across Event Hubs, Databricks, storage, and Key Vault — all in a two-day window. One real gap found and closed the next day: a missing personal read-access policy. The honest caveat: defined isn't the same as deployed. There's no evidence in this log that terraform apply ran, or that the live pipeline has moved off local Kafka yet. Week two wrote the plan. Running it is still ahead.
